chapter: Armstrong, Big Sid and Joe Glaser
title: Glaser's salary and the IOU slips that kept Louis solvent
summary: Louis had worked at Glaser's Sunset Cafe in Chicago before Erskine Tate, and Glaser put him on a salary with IOUs checked afterwards because his big heart gave everything away.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Were they friends before Joe bought his contract?

Well, Joe had worked for him -- I mean, Louie had worked for Louie -- I mean, for Joe because Joe had the Sunset Cafe in Chicago and he worked for Joe for a while. Then he went with a guy named Erskine Tate at a theater called the Vendome in Chicago. And that's when this guy -- I can't think of his name offhand -- and he picked Louie up and took him to Europe. And I don't know what happened between he and Louie but they couldn't get along evidently and that's when they had the fight and all that. So he wanted to teach Louie a lesson, get rid of him. So when he got back to Chicago he sold Louie to Joe, sold his contract.

And then Joe and Louie have been, ever since, buddy-buddy-buddy. Louie never did want for any money, you know, but he -- Joe gave him a salary. Because, you know, if you gave him all his money, he would give it away because he's so big-hearted. So he put him on a salary.
Now, if he wanted something, anything he wanted, and he didn't have enough money, then he'd borrow. See, he'd sign

an IOU slip like all the rest of us. See, when they'd get back to New York, then they'd check up on his IOU's and see how much money he borrowed, which didn't mean nothing, but that was to keep him straight, you know. And that's the only way they could keep Louie straight because them guys used to take him for -- they thought he was a sucker. He knew everything, but he didn't care. He'd call them all kind of names, anything.
